note: Set B is better because it avoids the significant duplication and entity typos ('Flexnoll' vs 'Flexinol') found in Set A. Both sets contain errors reading specific data points from the Nickel-Titanium chart (e.g., attributing -100°C to 51% or 53% instead of 52%), but Set B has fewer of these misreads and includes valid qualitative claims about the diagram labels and trends that Set A misses or renders vaguely.
remarks: Both sets struggle with the precise data points on the right-hand chart, likely due to image resolution; specifically, the -100°C point aligns with 52% Nickel Content, but both sets attribute it to 51% or 53%. Set A's duplication of claims (e.g., louver counts, force values) significantly reduces its quality.
